note: Editorial record for the LTTC research page. 'reported' holds numbers recorded at the time (each study's own validation set). 'models' lists ids re-scored afterwards on one held-out benchmark (rescored.json). 'direction.by' is a draft: owner, ai or unclear.

Input gain ×0.5.text: The guitar signal is scaled by 0.5, which is what the pedal's GAIN knob does at noon. The model is trained with the knob there.

Pre biquad.text: A small recursive filter with five coefficients, part of Valeton's SnapTone structure. It shapes the tone before the clipper.
Pre biquad.label: Biquad

Post biquad.text: The second recursive filter of Valeton's structure, after the clipper.
Post biquad.label: Biquad

Fixed biquad.text: Valeton's post-clipper biquad (from the same fixed filter set as the decimator), kept with fixed coefficients rather than learned.
Fixed biquad.label: Biquad

4× oversampling.text: Clipping creates harmonics far above the input's frequencies. At 44.1 kHz anything above 22 kHz folds back down as inharmonic aliasing. So the signal is first raised to 176.4 kHz by inserting three linearly interpolated points between each pair of samples; the clipper runs at that rate, and the decimator brings it back down.

Asymmetric exp clipper.text: A memoryless curve applied to every sample: nearly linear for small signals, flattening to a ceiling for large ones. Each side (positive, negative) has its own ceiling and steepness; the asymmetry adds even harmonics. Four learned numbers. The exponential is computed as (1 + z/1024)¹⁰²⁴ on the pedal.
Asymmetric exp clipper.label: Exp clipper

Learned-knee clipper.text: Like the exponential clipper, but an extra learned exponent p per side sets how sharp the bend into clipping is, from very soft (p small) to almost a hard clip (p large).

Learned curve 1.text: A free-form clipping curve: 33 fixed input points, spaced finely near zero and coarsely for loud signals (sinh spacing), each with a learned output value, joined by straight lines, with straight-line tails beyond the ends. The centre point is pinned at 0 so it can't add DC. This is one of LTTC's two "trained clippers". Between knots xᵢ ≤ x < xᵢ₊₁ the output is a straight line; the knots get further apart for louder signals.

Interstage FIR16 (at 4×).term: FIR filter between the clippers, 16 taps at 176.4 kHz
Interstage FIR16 (at 4×).text: A short filter between the two clipping curves, running at the oversampled rate. Like the tone stack between two gain stages of an amp, it changes which frequencies hit the second clipper hardest.
Interstage FIR16 (at 4×).label: FIR16

Decimate ↓4 (40-tap LPF).text: Brings the signal back from 176.4 kHz to 44.1 kHz: a 40-tap low-pass FIR (Valeton's, fixed) removes everything above about 20 kHz, then only every 4th sample is kept. The filter is what stops the clipper's high harmonics from aliasing.

Sum.text: The parallel branches above are added together, still at the oversampled rate, before the shared decimator.

Branch gain.text: The second branch is scaled by one learned number g before the sum. It starts small (0.05), so adding the branch doesn't change the model until training finds a use for it.
Branch gain.label: g

Output FIR256 + cab IR.term: FIR filter fused with a cabinet impulse response
Output FIR256 + cab IR.text: On the pedal, the learned 256-tap output filter and a 512-tap cabinet IR are both linear, so they're combined offline into one 767-tap filter: one convolution instead of two.
Output FIR256 + cab IR.label: FIR256 + cab IR

Tone controls & volume.text: The pedal's bass, middle, treble and volume knobs, as peaking and shelving biquad filters after the capture. Neutral at noon.
Tone controls & volume.label: Tone & volume

Extra clipping stages.text: Each arm of this campaign added something different after the parallel fronts: a bank of clipping curves, two or three more clippers in series, or a clipper whose bias follows the signal's envelope (the only one with memory).

Learned curve 2.text: A free-form clipping curve: 33 fixed input points, spaced finely near zero and coarsely for loud signals (sinh spacing), each with a learned output value, joined by straight lines, with straight-line tails beyond the ends. The centre point is pinned at 0 so it can't add DC. This is the second of LTTC's two "trained clippers". Between knots xᵢ ≤ x < xᵢ₊₁ the output is a straight line; the knots get further apart for louder signals.

Input FIR128.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 128 input samples, with 128 learned weights (taps). Before the clipper, it sets which frequencies get clipped hardest (like an amp's input stage). At 44.1 kHz, 128 taps cover 2.9 ms.
Input FIR128.label: FIR128

Input FIR32.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 32 input samples, with 32 learned weights (taps). Before the clipper, it sets which frequencies get clipped hardest (like an amp's input stage). At 44.1 kHz, 32 taps cover 0.7 ms.
Input FIR32.label: FIR32

Input FIR16.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 16 input samples, with 16 learned weights (taps). Before the clipper, it sets which frequencies get clipped hardest. At 44.1 kHz, 16 taps cover 0.4 ms.
Input FIR16.label: FIR16

Input FIR8.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 8 input samples, with 8 learned weights (taps). Before the clipper, it sets which frequencies get clipped hardest. At 44.1 kHz, 8 taps cover 0.2 ms.
Input FIR8.label: FIR8

Output FIR128.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 128 input samples, with 128 learned weights (taps). After the clipper, it shapes the final tone, including the speaker cabinet's response when the NAM captured a full rig. At 44.1 kHz, 128 taps cover 2.9 ms.
Output FIR128.label: FIR128

Output FIR256.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 256 input samples, with 256 learned weights (taps). After the clipper, it shapes the final tone, including the speaker cabinet's response when the NAM captured a full rig. At 44.1 kHz, 256 taps cover 5.8 ms.
Output FIR256.label: FIR256

Output FIR512.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 512 input samples, with 512 learned weights (taps). After the clipper, it shapes the final tone, including the speaker cabinet's response when the NAM captured a full rig. At 44.1 kHz, 512 taps cover 11.6 ms.
Output FIR512.label: FIR512

Output FIR768.text: A finite impulse response filter: each output sample is a weighted sum of the last 768 input samples, with 768 learned weights (taps). After the clipper, it shapes the final tone, including the speaker cabinet's response when the NAM captured a full rig. At 44.1 kHz, 768 taps cover 17.4 ms.
Output FIR768.label: FIR768

milestones.title: Recover the SnapTone baseline
milestones.summary: Decode Suite-generated SnapTone records, reproduce Valeton's renderer offline and score the stock model before trying to beat it. Refitting the same structure ourselves already beats Suite's fit.
milestones.changed: Starting point: Valeton's own capture structure.

training.optimizer: Suite's fit (SnapTone); Adam for our refit
training.data: NAM Core's sample A2 model on Suite's own capture signal

direction.note: Part of the agreed plan to measure the stock capture first.

milestones.title: Try beyond the stock structure
milestones.summary: Screen longer output filters, filtered cascades, other clipping curves and a small residual TCN on the same data.
milestones.changed: Explored new structures; extra nonlinear stages and the TCN did not reliably help.

training.data: Guitar section of Suite's capture signal, NAM Core's sample A2 model

direction.note: Owner asked for strong offline candidates; the agent chose the structures.

milestones.title: Fit real playing; extend the tail
milestones.summary: Switch to the owner's DI recordings at their real input level and compare the stock-length output filter with a 768-tap one.
milestones.changed: Real guitar DI instead of synthetic signals; output FIR 512 → 768 taps.

training.data: Guitar section of Suite's capture signal (per the run's result.json)

direction.note: Owner supplied the DI recordings and found the 768-tap version hard to tell from the teacher.

milestones.title: Candidate B becomes the lead
milestones.summary: Balance PRS fingerstyle, PRS pick and JSM10 pick across training and validation, then freeze a three-candidate shortlist before scoring.
milestones.changed: Training data mixes two guitars and two playing styles; candidate B (FIR768) is chosen.

direction.note: Owner suggested mixing guitars and styles, and preferred B by ear.

milestones.title: One architecture, three amps
milestones.summary: Fit candidate B to three new NAM teachers: a bright clean amp, a Marshall and a Peavey 5150. The Peavey is clearly the hardest.
milestones.changed: Three teacher amps instead of one; same architecture.

direction.note: Multi-teacher check; unclear who proposed it.

milestones.title: Learn the clipping curve's shape
milestones.summary: Longer fits, wider initializations, a learned smooth-to-hard curve and a two-stage cascade on all three amps.
milestones.changed: Clipping curve gets learnable knees; filtered two-stage cascade tried.

direction.note: Overnight agent research.

milestones.title: A stronger Peavey seed
milestones.summary: Restart the Peavey from the best wide initialization; compare the exponential curve with a learned shape and a 33-knot monotone curve.
milestones.changed: Better starting point; first 33-knot curve tried (later reused in LTTC).

direction.note: Agent follow-up of 022.

milestones.title: Chase the missing brightness
milestones.summary: The Peavey still sounds dull. Test EQ-augmented training, frequency-weighted losses and level-dependent (compressor/state) variants.
milestones.changed: Training data and loss aimed at high frequencies; dynamic variants tried.

direction.note: Driven by the owner hearing the Peavey as dull.

milestones.title: Parallel clipping fronts
milestones.summary: Check oversampling quality, then add a second filtered clipping branch summed at 4× before the shared decimator.
milestones.changed: Second nonlinear branch in parallel (FIR + curve), summed at 4×.

direction.note: Agent structural study.

milestones.title: Train on the high band directly
milestones.summary: Add a loss term on high-band magnitude mismatch to the parallel-front model.
milestones.changed: Loss: extra high-band magnitude term.

direction.note: Follow-up of the brightness complaint.

milestones.title: Focus on abrasive upper mids
milestones.summary: Target the upper-mid region with its own loss, optionally with an extra static or filtered stage.
milestones.changed: Loss: upper-mid term; extra stage variants.

direction.note: Follow-up of listening notes on the Peavey.

milestones.title: Make fitting practical
milestones.summary: Compare ordinary joint training with periodic least-squares refits of the output filter, to cut fitting time.
milestones.changed: Training recipe only (periodic least-squares tried); joint Adam kept.

direction.note: Needed for a user-facing trainer.

milestones.title: Shrink the filters
milestones.summary: Cut the filters to fit the pedal: output FIR 768 → 384 → 256, and compact fronts of 32 and 16 taps.
milestones.changed: Compact geometry: FIR32 + FIR16 fronts, 256-tap output FIR.

direction.note: Owner asked for cheaper captures that leave room for an IR.

milestones.title: Give compact more training
milestones.summary: Continue the compact model for 900 more updates to see how much of the gap to full size is just training budget.
milestones.changed: Longer training of the compact model.

direction.note: Agent overnight queue.

milestones.title: Train on a perceptual metric
milestones.summary: Ask which distances track hearing, then train full, compact and tiny models on the paper-supported MFCC distance.
milestones.changed: Loss: PaperMFCC. Scores from here on are MFCC, not ESR.

direction.note: Owner pointed to perceptual metrics and the paper behind the MFCC distance.

milestones.title: Tiny stays out of reach
milestones.summary: Fix the tiny model's initialization; it improves but stays far from acceptable on the Peavey. Kept as a negative result.
milestones.changed: Tiny geometry (FIR16 / FIR8 → 128) with a better start.

direction.note: Agent follow-up.

milestones.title: Compact goes to the pedal
milestones.summary: Owner listening favours compact. Build it as a pedal effect (GPTC record, ARM loader, DSP kernel) and fuse an IR into the output filter.
milestones.changed: Same model, now running on the GP-50.

direction.note: Owner's listening verdict and request for the pedal implementation.

milestones.title: A trainer anyone can run
milestones.summary: NAM A2 Full → compact fitting with no research checkpoints: a generic 15-start initialization, then Adam on MFCC. Later moved fully into the browser.
milestones.changed: Training recipe: cold start from any NAM, on the user's machine. First runs are short (180 updates).

training.data: Any 1–8 DIs × 3 drives, first 60 s each

direction.note: Owner asked for browser-side NAM → capture fitting.

milestones.title: New teachers, longer runs
milestones.summary: Fender, Soldano and Vox teachers trained with the trainer at 1,800 updates; Soldano sounds too bright.
milestones.changed: Same recipe, 10× the updates, new teachers.

direction.note: Owner requested the three teachers.

milestones.title: Train to a plateau
milestones.summary: Owner corrects premature fixed-budget stopping: continue Soldano fits until validation stops improving.
milestones.changed: Stopping rule: validation plateau instead of a fixed budget.

direction.note: Owner corrected the stopping policy.

milestones.title: Nine new amps and pedals
milestones.summary: Download nine A2 Full teachers from Tone3000 (Marshall, Friedman, Orange, JC120, Klon, RAT, a Fuzz Factory clone…) and fit each with the trainer, then continue to a plateau. The fuzz and the RAT end far behind the amps.
milestones.changed: Much wider set of teachers; plateau continuation.

direction.note: Owner chose the collection and authorized the downloads.

milestones.title: The real Fuzz Factory
milestones.summary: The clone turned out not to be the popular reference, so the genuine Z.Vex Fuzz Factory (Vexter) is added. It needs a much higher-gain initialization screen (drive up to 131,072) before training gets anywhere.
milestones.changed: New hardest teacher; initialization screen extended to very high drive.

direction.note: Owner asked for a genuine Fuzz Factory run with a high-gain initialization.

milestones.title: More clipping stages
milestones.summary: The fuzz pedals and the RAT are stuck far behind the amps. Try a bank of parallel clipping curves, two or three serial clipping stages, or envelope-biased clipping, on the Fuzz Factory, its clone, the RAT and the Marshall.
milestones.changed: Extra clipping stages around the compact front.

direction.note: Agent-proposed architecture campaign, motivated by the poor fuzz and RAT fits.

milestones.title: Learn the whole curve
milestones.summary: Replace the entire nonlinear front with one or two learned 33-knot curves (with a 16-tap filter between them), trained to a plateau. The big gains are on the fuzz pedals: the Fuzz Factory drops from 10.1 to 6.8.
milestones.changed: Nonlinearity: free-form learned curves replace exponentials and branches. Two curves = the future LTTC.

direction.note: Agent proposed; owner asked to run it.

milestones.title: LTTC: two curves on the pedal, from scratch
milestones.summary: Port the two-curve model to the pedal as a new record format, and give the trainer a from-scratch recipe. An optimizer survey finds nothing that beats Adam outright.
milestones.changed: Released architecture (Lean Twin Trained Clippers); trained from a cold start instead of a warm start.

direction.note: Owner: "let's port the two spline capture".

milestones.title: Schedule-free AdamW
milestones.summary: Schedule-free AdamW reaches plain Adam's 4,000-step score in about 1,000 steps; it becomes the trainer default.
milestones.changed: Optimizer: schedule-free AdamW.

direction.note: From the agent's optimizer literature survey.

milestones.title: Released
milestones.summary: Peppercorn v0.1.0 ships LTTC captures. The released Peavey capture is compared with Suite's SnapTone and the NAM on the pedal.
milestones.changed: Release; Peavey retrained with the final recipe. A shorter 900-update budget is checked for the website trainer.

direction.note: Release decision.
